react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, mummichog empirical-compound network, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converged on C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP returned FDR 2.16e-14 for SMPDB SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) and KEGG map00140, with a fold-enrichment of 1250; the same five steroid inputs (androstenedione, testosterone, DHEA, estradiol, and 5α-dihydrotestosterone) also populated the WikiPathways and Reactome steroidogenesis maps at ranks 4–7. Mummichog independently ranked the C21-steroid hormone pathway first by empirical p-value 0.00168, with a perfect 10-of-10 overlap from the steroid input set — the highest possible network coverage. MetaboAnalystR confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 as the top KEGG-only hit, reinforcing the cross-paradigm consensus. The prostaglandin formation from arachidonate pathway also surfaced (mummichog rank 2, p=0.023), driven by thromboxane A₂ (ChEBI:15627), linking the observed changes to platelet activation and vascular tone regulation. Secondary weaker hits included tryptophan metabolism (quinolinic acid, p=0.068) and ascorbate/aldarate metabolism (dehydroascorbic acid, p=0.047). The five steroid hormones — androstenedione (C00280), testosterone (C00535), DHEA (C01227), estradiol (C00951), and 5α-dihydrotestosterone (C03917) — are the primary drivers, collectively occupying ≥9 pathway memberships and anchoring a coherent story of sex-steroid flux across treatment conditions.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-database ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways) ranked 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150) and 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (REACT:R-HSA-196071) as the top hits with FDR ≈ 2.16×10⁻¹⁴ and fold-enrichment ≈ 1250. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently returned hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) as its top hit with 5 of 5 input steroids mapped. Mummichog's m/z-directed network analysis ranked 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' first (p=0.0014) with 10/10 input steroids overlapping, and 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' second (p=0.0024). A secondary thromboxane/prostaglandin signal emerged from m/z analysis (MUMM:prostaglandin formation from arachidonate, p=0.018), supported by thromboxane itself (KEGG:C02198) as a pathway member. The six steroid driver metabolites—dehydroepiandrosterone, androstenedione, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, androstenedione, and estradiol—each map directly to the androgen/estrogen biosynthesis pathway members confirmed by RaMP and verified by Mummichog overlap. Quinolinic acid and dehydroascorbic acid appear in peripheral pathway hits (tryptophan metabolism, ascorbate metabolism) but do not reach consensus rank ≤5 across paradigms. The strong five-steroid convergence across ORA and network paradigms indicates pervasive dysregulation of the gonadal steroid axis in the treatment condition.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The ten differentially abundant metabolites resolve into two dominant and one secondary biological signal across three independent enrichment paradigms. The primary and overwhelmingly dominant signal is steroid hormone metabolism: five input steroids (testosterone, androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone, dihydrotestosterone, and estradiol) produce a highly significant enrichment for Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150, RaMP FDR 2.16e-14) and the broader Metabolism of steroid hormones (REACT:R-HSA-196071, RaMP FDR 1.10e-13). This pathway is independently recovered as the top Mummichog hit (MUMM:C21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=0.00218, 10/10 steroid compounds overlapping) and as MetaboAnalystR's top KEGG hit (hsa00140, p=1.0). Five steroid compounds act as driver metabolites, mapping to both androgen and estrogen branches of the canonical steroidogenesis cascade. The secondary signal is prostaglandin formation: thromboxane (KEGG:C02198) drives Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (MUMM, p=0.0218, rank 2) and Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM, p=0.0492, rank 6). A tertiary, weaker signal implicates ascorbate metabolism (dehydroascorbic acid, MUMM rank 3, p=0.0388) and nicotinamide metabolism via quinolinic acid (MUMM rank 4, p=0.0492). Dobutamine and 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutaric acid did not enrich any pathway above significance thresholds.
